answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce stake before submitting jobs, with rewards released only after peers verify useful work. A randomly chosen kernel of reviewers checks outputs; failed claims forfeit stake. Making many identities therefore costs capital per account, and the attacker risks losing it when caught. Reputation earned across tasks raises the cost of replacing exposed accounts. Even at the summit, pigment-based identity clues cannot substitute for costly stake and verification.
